name: Must explicitly name the NullPointerException vs generic null-safety language (guard/robustness) suffices
side_a: Credit only if the answer explicitly names the exception (e.g., 'NullPointerException' / 'NPE') as the consequence of the null access; generic advice to 'guard against null' or make the code 'robust against null assignments' without naming the exception does not count as discussing the possible NPE — deduct 1 point.
side_b: Credit any answer that raises the null-dereference risk in substance, even if it never names NullPointerException — recommending a null guard or saying the field 'can be null' implies the exception, so no deduction.
